Sampled recommendation metrics can reverse model comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation, even in expectation; fixing negatives improves paired comparability but does not remove sampling bias ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). For history-perturbation diagnostics, a recommended design is to sample unique negatives once per pair, excluding the target and the union of original and replacement history items, then reuse identical candidates for both histories. This prevents candidate/history overlap and changing competitor difficulty from contaminating the measured effect. Union exclusion changes the eligible catalog, so describe results as conditional diagnostic effects and preserve the pinned benchmark separately.

Tie handling must be explicit. With g negatives scoring above the target and e equal-scoring negatives, optimistic rank is 1+g, pessimistic rank 1+g+e, and midrank 1+g+e/2 ([PyKEEN documentation](https://pykeen.readthedocs.io/en/v1.1.0/tutorial/understanding_evaluation.html)). Target-first stable sorting can favor the target under ties. Averaging metric values over tied permutations avoids arbitrary ordering; reciprocal midrank generally differs from average reciprocal rank across those permutations ([McSherry and Najork](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/computing-information-retrieval-performance-measures-efficiently-in-the-presence-of-tied-scores/)). Match benchmark conventions when reproducing benchmark scores.

For one target, HR@10 = 1[r≤10], reciprocal rank = 1/r. Define paired changes consistently as perturbed minus original. HR changes capture crossings of the tenth-place boundary; reciprocal-rank changes capture movements throughout the ranking, emphasizing early positions. Unchanged HR with lower reciprocal rank can therefore indicate deterioration within either side of the cutoff. Report paired means, uncertainty, tie frequency, and whether reciprocal rank is truncated. These measure sensitivity to a specified intervention, not benchmark improvement or causal preference effects.
